title: Fee growth cap for services taking the early childhood worker retention payment
summary: Services that opt into the worker retention payment must limit fee growth to 4.4% from 8 August 2024 to 7 August 2025, then 4.2%.

instruments.title: Early childhood worker retention payment grant conditions

commenced.what: Fee growth cap applies to opted-in services

direction_rationale: A cap restrains fee growth for opted-in services but may slow expansion and entry where costs rise faster.
confounders: Cheaper Child Care subsidy increase 10 Jul 2023

assessment.summary: Services taking the worker retention payment must hold fee growth to about 4.4% a year. It funds higher pay for educators but caps prices for services whose costs rise faster, which may slow expansion.

marks.reason: A cap on fee growth ties prices to a set rate rather than to each service's costs.
Capped revenue growth lowers the expected return on new or expanded centres.
The payment funds a wage rise that helps attract and keep qualified educators.
